positions.title: Technology Analyst - Eq. Derivs. IT, Trading and Execution Engineering
positions.locationName: New York, New York, United States
positions.description:
Scored 1st in the Americas and 2nd in the World in the Credit Suisse Global Coding Challenge.

Developed a service that parses an xlsx request for quote (RFQ) and produces as output a json data payload. RFQs are client-specific and highly complex, often entailing multiple tables, joins across tables, strike/price multipliers, date arithmetic, nested headers, different financial derivatives, and so on, all of which needed to be completely configurable. [Java]

Developed an application in React and Redux that integrates with the above service, with an interactive grid that provides many of the same rich selection capabilities and keyboard shortcuts as Excel. [React/Redux, Jest/Enzyme]

positions.title: Summer Technology Analyst - Equity Derivatives IT
positions.locationName: New York, New York, United States
positions.description:
Developed a new workflow across the stack and implemented realtime notifications within the Credit Suisse structured notes pricing application (SPRITE) to allow sales and trading to reprice notes and conduct the entire deal-making procedure. [C#, JS/Angular]

Created a Blockchain application to reliably track SLAs and OLAs across the firm. [Corda, JS/Node]

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Developed a highly versatile long-term option strategy backtesting system entirely in C/C++. Computed historical volatility and greeks from scratch using CBOE raw option data and Black-Scholes. The system was extensible to a wide variety of securities, option strategies, and technical indicators, and capable of conducting fast tests on 12+ years of daily and weekly option data.

Developed a full-stack web application to display stocks (and options, futures, warrants, etc.) with positions, prices, and a variety of other statistics in realtime. Built a system across the stack, using Java (with JDBC and the TraderWorkstation API), mySQL, PHP, JS (with AJAX), and HTML.

positions.title: Founder and CTO
positions.description:
Promly was a social and e-commerce platform for school dances using AWS, Parse, Node.js, Materialize, and everything in-between. 

Received multiple seed funding offers, with a maximum offer of $100,000, and a maximum pre-money valuation of $500,000.

honors.title: Gold Perfy (Performance Optimization), Sweety (GenAI), Healthy (Code Health) Awards H2 2026
honors.description: Awarded for developing Google's first agentic evolutionary optimization framework and applying it to land over $6M in resource savings as well as numerous improvements in YouTube client application performance, test runtimes, server latency, and more.

honors.title: Gold "Sweety" (Gen AI) Award H1 2025
honors.description: Awarded for developing a generic GenAI-powered log summarization service and applying it to explain operation failures in Google/YouTube’s video processing engine.

projects.title: MoleML
projects.description:
App for detecting Melanoma and Basal Cell Carcinoma using OpenCV/Machine Learning:
MoleML is a cross-platform mobile application which puts the power of machine learning into the hands of everyday users. MoleML allows users to take or submit a picture of a mole that they suspect is cancerous. A self-developed algorithm analyzes the image and makes a prediction whether or not the mole is cancerous, also providing a confidence level. The algorithm uses Random Forest Classification and OpenCV (to detect 13 image characteristics along with 5 clinical characteristics) to detect skin cancer with 86% accuracy. MoleML then allows users to track their moles over time, providing data and graphs as visual aids to help determine whether or not the moles are becoming more dangerous.
